name_devanagari: अजयमेरुकोट मन्दिर समूह १, शिखर डेवल २ || DDL0113
description_en: A śikhara temple from circa 14th century.Ajayamerukoṭa is situated 4 km north-west of Amargaḍhī, the Dadeldhura district headquarters. Most of the monuments of the area are built on the right bank of the Chaurī Gāḍ river, an affluent of the Mahakali (or Sharda) river, that makes the western river between India and Nepal. Theśikharatemple is located on a terrace where other contemporary constructions are standing (DDL0110, DDL0111 and DDL0113).The area of Ajayamerukoṭa is rich in monuments that were mostly erected during the 14th and 15th centuries. According to D. P. Ojha, Ajayamerukoṭa was a local capital of the Khasiya kings from Jumla, (i.e. the Khaśa Malla emperors, 12th-14th century) (Ojha 1989: p. 54). From the mid-14th century, Ajayamerukoṭa seems to have taken greater importance as a capital of the Doti kingdom, especially under the reign of king Niraya Pāla (r. c. 1362-1383 CE). Indeed, it is around Niraya Pāla's time that Doti emerged as an entity independant from the Khaśa Malla empire. This political and economical rise is demonstrated in the numerous monuments erected between the second half of the 14th century and throughout the 15th century.This free standingśikharatemple is part of a temple complex counting two pairs ofśikharatemples with a central pavilion (DDL0110,DDL0111), a small, half-buriedśikhara(DDL0112) and a pavilion (DDL0120). It is identical in style to the nearbyśikhara. The façades are richly decorated with blind niches, diamond motifs (losanges) and Kīrtimukha. The top of the tower is crowned by a large stoneāmalakadisc. The pediment of the temple was recently restored, with newly carved blocks added to it.Despite the few available elements, it is possible to suggest that the temple was built around the second half of the 14th century (nearbyśikharatemples with an almost identical pavilion are dated from 1373 CE (ŚS 1295), seeSharma 2012: p. 303).
references: REFERENCES Ojha, D. P. 1988. Doti Kṣetrako Itihās tathā Saṃnskrīti . Kathmandu: Sudur Paścimāncal Sāmājik Sevā tathā Anusandhān Samiti. Sharma, Dilli Raj. 2012. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies.
